title: Sampled token-span tracing and aggregation pipeline for token-level cost attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a low-overhead, sampled tracing pipeline that emits token-level spans and aggregates them into rollups for cost and latency attribution. The goal is to enable engineers and PMs to answer: how much latency and token-cost is attributable to model decoding vs KV cache retrieval vs I/O, with minimal overhead in production. This ticket spans runtime hooks, OTLP-compatible span enrichment, sampling strategy, aggregation consumer, and Grafana dashboard panels.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a sampled token-span for decode and KV-access phases with stable span names/attributes
Span payloads follow our OTEL/OTLP attribute schema (trace_id, request_id, model_variant, token_index, cache_hit:boolean, seq_len_bucket)
Sampling reduces telemetry event rate to <1% of tokens for 95th percentile workloads while preserving accuracy for top-k rollups
Aggregation pipeline produces hourly/day rollups by model_variant and route with approximate per-token latency and cost estimates
Grafana dashboard has token-level latency breakdown and cache-impact panels; panels refresh within 5m of ingestion
End-to-end validation doc with synthetic workload and live A/B shows <5% instrumentation overhead on p95 latency
implementation_plan: Design phase: finalize span schema and sampling algorithm (adaptive reservoir + stratified by model_variant and seq_len)
Runtime changes: add tracing hook points in decoder loop and KV fetch path; make hooks no-op unless sampling flag enabled
Telemetry: emit spans via OTLP exporter to Kafka/OTLP bridge; include proto-compatible attributes to avoid downstream parsing work
Aggregation: consumer job will join spans by trace_id/request_id and produce rollups (per hour) stored in metrics-store (Timescale/ClickHouse) and lightweight daily assets in BigQuery
Dashboards: build Grafana dashboard and panels; wire up templating for model_variant and region
Validation: run synthetic tests, deploy canary, compare aggregated numbers to high-fidelity non-sampled run to calibrate sampling factors
Rollout: enable sampling at 0.1% initially, monitor overhead/utility, then increase/adjust stratification as needed
notes: We must avoid emitting a span per-token in hot paths. Sampling + deterministic hash (based on request_id and token_index) suggested to ensure reproducible selection and easy join semantics.
KV cache instrumentation should tag whether the fetch was local GPU memory vs remote parameter server to capture network cost delta.
Consider exporting a compact summary span for un-sampled requests so downstream joins can still place tokens in sequence context without full traces.
Pricing model: need to surface estimated per-token cost using token count * unit-cost model; consult billing team for cost-per-token constants.
Storage: hourly rollups kept at high cardinality (model_variant, route, cache_hit) but aggregated by seq_len_bucket to bound cardinality. Keep retention policy aligned with console analytics TTL.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: instrumentation increases p95 latency if implemented synchronously. Mitigation: async OTLP exporter with bounded ring buffer and backpressure metrics; ensure hook is lock-free and inlined.
Risk: sampling bias on small customers. Mitigation: stratified sampling and a short-lived deterministic override in dev/qa for full traces.
Risk: high cardinality in aggregation. Mitigation: enforce seq_len bucketing, model_variant normalization, and configurable sample keys.
Risk: cost calculation mismatch with billing. Mitigation: add reconciliation job comparing estimate to billing records weekly and surface diffs in console.
Risk: security/PII in spans. Mitigation: attribute whitelist and hashing of any identifiers; security review required (flagged).
